roles.design_prompt: Dry close studio mic. A woman around thirty with a clear mid-register voice, native American English. A focused observer speaking to the one teammate she trusts. Measured, economical delivery, fine precise consonants, a hint of a smile when relieved. Let the important word land, then drop the pitch at the end. Calm even when tracking a fast target, with an intimate, human sound.
roles.mix: OF-04 helmet radio, 350–4350 Hz main band, thin hiss, higher key tone

roles.design_prompt: Dry close studio mic. A man in his early thirties with a compact, chesty mid-low speaking voice, native American English. He's the teammate at the front who turns to talk over his shoulder. The voice catches a little on the first consonant; a little breath escapes after a hard stop. Short, physical phrases, restless energy, warmth under pressure. Clearly articulated at conversational volume, with space for an urgent call to cut through.
roles.mix: OF-04 helmet radio, 240–3450 Hz main band, stronger squelch, low key tone

roles.design_prompt: Clean studio sound. A resonant, low-pitched androgynous contralto with a light standard southern British accent. The friendly onboard tactical operator of a science fiction arena. Even pulses of speech, small precise pauses at clause boundaries, a restrained pitch contour and a soft downward cadence. Cool, lucid, reassuring authority. Intelligible pure speech with a subtle almost synthetic regularity.
roles.mix: 14-band vocoder, 112/168 Hz carriers, 41 Hz ring modulation blended with clean speech; two-tone link cue
